attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post. They are not quoted from anyone else.

semantics.note: An unhedged present-tense claim that LLMs lack outcomes that would make a 3x to 10x price rise tenable. The normalised wording keeps the multiples and the scope.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary: would repeatable net benefits sustain 3x, 4x or 10x prices? The baseline price, breadth of adoption and meaning of 'tenable' are supplied by the evaluator, so interpretation drives the result.

evidence.note: Klarna's own filing reports AI support savings and faster resolutions. It is a company disclosure with no model-cost baseline or price-multiple analysis, so it cannot settle tenability.
METR's RCT found a slowdown in one narrow coding setting, early 2025. It has no price or cost analysis and METR says the result is out of date.
METR's follow-up suggests a likely speedup but calls its own data weak evidence. It does not address price multiples.

reviews.rationale: None of the items compares realised net benefits with costs at 3x, 4x or 10x prices. Klarna's savings are a company disclosure without model-cost data, and the METR studies are narrow productivity measures. The packet neither supports nor contradicts the claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his post.

semantics.note: The sentence before calls 'LLMs being able to write all code' a myth, so 'can write all code' is a concession made for argument. The normalised wording presents it as an asserted capability. The real commitment is that generating code does not guarantee quality, readability or value.

contract.note: The contract rightly treats the core as a non-implication and does not score the concession. Its support condition is modest, which matches the speaker's limited claim.

evidence.note: Benchmark released 16 March 2026, inside the window. Of 54 complete-program attempts by frontier models, 21 scored zero on gate failures, so generated code was often not functionally adequate.
Anthropic's own February 2026 demonstration of a generated compiler, listing efficiency and quality limits. It is a company disclosure dated before the target period.

reviews.rationale: The core claim is that generating code does not by itself make the code good. An independent March 2026 benchmark shows complete generated programs often failing basic gates. Readability and long-term business effects are not measured, but the contract does not require them. The 'can write all code' concession is not scored.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: 'Will' makes the data-centre-centred crisis in 2026 or 2027 a firm forecast. The pension and insurance harm is only a worry, and the normalised wording correctly keeps it hedged ('could').

contract.note: Reading it as a systemic crisis with data-centre debt central, by 31 December 2027, is ordinary and fair. The early-resolution rule is reasonable.

evidence.note: IMF blog of 13 October 2026, before the evaluation date. It describes resilient markets and only prospective AI-related risks. It records no crisis that has happened.

reviews.rationale: The deadline is 31 December 2027, after the evaluation date. No dated systemic crisis centred on data-centre debt appears in the evidence, so the early-resolution rule is not met. The absence of a crisis so far is not failure.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his post.

semantics.note: 'Undoubtedly' makes this a firm conditional forecast: a fee rise to 2 to 5 times today's level leads to massive churn. Tagging 'cover costs' as source wording is inference, but the contract treats it as context only.

contract.note: An imposed 2x to 5x rise for comparable existing plans, followed by large sustained cancellations, is a fair ordinary reading. No churn threshold or follow-up window is given.

evidence.note: TechRadar, 16 June 2026: ChatGPT Plus and Pro prices unchanged. This suggests the antecedent had not occurred for those plans. It does not cover all plans or the period up to October.

reviews.rationale: No qualifying 2x to 5x fee increase is documented, so the antecedent is unmet or unknown and the conditional cannot be scored. No deadline was stated.
